pages.hook: In the USA, a party starts with an invitation and a short reply. Learn the little words that make you a great guest, from RSVP to what to bring.
pages.polite: Always answer an invitation. Say **Thanks for the invite!** and ask **Can I bring something?**

mythfact.s: RSVP means “please reply to the invitation”.
mythfact.why: It comes from the French “répondez, s’il vous plaît”.

mythfact.s: It is rude to ask, “Can I bring something?”
mythfact.why: It is polite. Hosts often say, “Just a drink or a snack!”

mythfact.s: At a potluck, each guest brings a dish to share.
mythfact.why: A potluck is a meal where everybody brings some food.

mythfact.s: At a birthday party, people never sing.
mythfact.why: People usually sing “Happy Birthday to You” and the person blows out candles.

mythfact.s: You can say “I can’t come” to an invitation.
mythfact.why: A short, kind “no” is fine: “I’d love to, but I’m busy.”

lines: **Maya’s Birthday Party**
Saturday, May 10 · 7:00 PM
123 Oak Street · Please RSVP by Thursday

decode.why: The card says Saturday, May 10, 7:00 PM.

lines: Hi Lina! Thanks for the invite.
I’d love to come! Can I bring something?
I can make a salad. See you Saturday!

compare.br: In Brazil, friends often just show up and the host does the cooking; a guest may arrive later than the invitation time.
compare.us: In the USA, guests usually reply to the invitation and often bring a drink or a snack to share.
compare.tip: Asking “Can I bring something?” is a kind way to say thank you before the party.
compare.ask: Do you bring something to a party where you live? What do you bring? Say it in English.

quiz.q: Lina says, “Can you come to my party?” You want to go. You say…
quiz.why: Accept and ask for the time.

quiz.q: What does RSVP ask you to do?
A host says “A drink or a snack.” You bring…

pages.title: Reading quest — Come to my party! · part 1
text: Hi Nia, **it’ll be fun**! I am having a party on Saturday at eight. It is a small party at my house, and I want you to come.
The address is 123 Oak Street in Oakland. **Can I bring something?** you ask. Sure! A drink or a snack is great. I will make pizza and a big cake. A cake with a bowl of fruit is my favorite.
We will play music and dance. Some friends play games. At nine, we will sing “Happy Birthday” and the birthday girl will blow out the candles. We say “**Cheers!**” and raise our cups.

fast.why: Lina invites Nia to a party.

text: Do you know the old rhyme “Pat-a-Cake”? It is an English nursery rhyme from a play of 1698. Children clap and say, “Bake me a cake as fast as you can.” My little brother loves it, and he will sing it at the party.

pages.title: Reading quest · Talk about it
text: Hi Nia, **it’ll be fun**! I am having a party on Saturday at eight. It is a small party at my house, and I want you to come.
The address is 123 Oak Street in Oakland. **Can I bring something?** you ask. Sure! A drink or a snack is great. I will make pizza and a big cake. A cake with a bowl of fruit is my favorite.
We will play music and dance. Some friends play games. At nine, we will sing “Happy Birthday” and the birthday girl will blow out the candles. We say “**Cheers!**” and raise our cups.

Do you know the old rhyme “Pat-a-Cake”? It is an English nursery rhyme from a play of 1698. Children clap and say, “Bake me a cake as fast as you can.” My little brother loves it, and he will sing it at the party.
Please tell me by Thursday. Can you come? If you can’t, **I’d love to see you next time**. **Thanks for the invite** is all you need to say. **See you Saturday!**
